diagnosed: Two real, reproducible breakages, both with their root-cause fix in .github/workflows/** — which the protect-automation safety hook (CI-only) blocks any unattended agent from authoring. (1) Research agent: EVERY workflow_dispatch run fails with 'Workflow initiated by non-human actor: github-actions (type: Bot). Add bot to allowed_bots list or use *'; scheduled runs succeed. Cause: scout/coverage-critic escalations dispatch research-agent.yml via escalate-research.js using the job GITHUB_TOKEN (github-actions bot), and anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 now rejects bot actors unless allow-listed. The entire deep-tier escalation path is dead. (2) Visual QA agent: EVERY scheduled run since 2026-08-31 fails on 'Claude reported a successful result after 50 turns, exceeding the configured maximum of 40' — the QA work actually completes and commits visual-qa-log.json (e.g. commit be3bcf990), then the action marks the run failed for exceeding --max-turns 40. Reading three full-page screenshots via scroll increments now legitimately needs >40 turns.
notes: Not quota: usage-state.json is green (0% used, skipAll:false). Not tests: npm test green (1537 passing). Not validation: validate-events.js reports 0 errors (only data-content warnings, which are the verify agent's job). Not publish: publish-freshness.json status 'fresh'.

FIX 1 (research-agent.yml): add `allowed_bots: "github-actions"` under `with:` in all three anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 steps (standard Opus, deep Fable, deep Opus fallback). This re-enables scout/coverage-critic deep-tier escalations. github-actions is the only legitimate dispatcher (via escalate-research.js), so allow-list it specifically rather than '*'.

FIX 2 (visual-qa-agent.yml): raise `--max-turns 40` to `--max-turns 80` in the claude_args of the claude-code-action step. The task completes at ~50 turns and the 15-min timeout is not the bottleneck (runs finish in ~5 min); the turn cap is the only thing turning a successful, committed QA run into a red failure.

BLOCKED from authoring both fixes: scripts/hooks/protect-automation.js exits 2 on any Write/Edit/Bash mutation of .github/workflows/** when GITHUB_ACTIONS/CI is set (both are true here). Its design is explicit that even the self-fixing loops must not author protected-path changes — 'a protected-path change must be authored by a human, not any unattended agent'. So no branch/PR was opened; a human operator must apply the two one-line-class edits above (they will still land as a reviewable, revertable commit).
